title: Microsoft Teams: Expanded Markdown support in the compose box
summary: Microsoft Teams will launch an expanded Markdown compose experience in early December 2026, allowing users to write with visible Markdown syntax, use a dedicated toolbar, preview messages before sending, and switch between Markdown and rich text. No admin action is needed.
body:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is introducing an updated Markdown compose experience with expanded formatting support. Users can write and edit with Markdown syntax intact, without formatting automatically rendering as they type. A dedicated Markdown toolbar helps users insert formatting syntax, preview the rendered message before sending, and switch between Markdown and rich text.

[Rollout schedule]

- General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

- Microsoft Teams users who compose messages in chats and channels on supported platformsPlatforms and services

- Microsoft Teams for Windows, Mac, and webWhat will happen

Users will be able to select Format in Markdown from the compose box’s Actions and apps (+) menu (Screenshot 1).

The updated experience includes:

- Markdown authoring without live rendering: Syntax remains visible and editable while users write.- A dedicated Markdown toolbar: Users can insert syntax for formatting (Screenshot 2).

- Message preview: Users can turn on Preview message to see the rendered formatting before sending (Screenshot 3).

- Switching between compose modes: Users can select Format in rich text from the same menu to return to rich text authoring (Screenshot 4).- Teams will remember the user’s selected compose mode and apply it across chats and channels until the user switches modes.

Learn more

- Use Markdown formatting in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required to prepare for this feature.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
